newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Generale Bank still looking for German acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Generale Bank still looking for German acquisition.

text.p: Generale Bank, Belgium's biggest bank, is still looking to buy a bank in North-Rhine-Westphalia (NRW), the eastern German state which borders on Belgium, the bank said on Tuesday.
"At a geographical level, we are still interested in acquiring a bank in NRW," chief executive officer Ferdinand Chaffart told a news conference.
Chaffart said Generale Bank had become even more interested in Germany since its 22 billion franc acquisition of Credit Lyonnais Bank Nederland (the Netherlands' fourth-biggest bank) last year.
Generale Bank has a strategy of expanding in a 400 kilometre radius around its Brussels headquarters.
Sixty percent of the bank's 7.3 billion franc first-half 1996 group net profit was earned abroad, 40 percent in the neighbouring countries France, the Netherlands, Luxembourg and Germany.
Chaffart said Generale Bank was looking for a bank with a good customer base in small and medium sized companies and 20 to 30 branch offices in NRW.
"Unfortunately, we cannot find anything which is attractive enough in NRW," Chaffart said.
"It may be a search without success. In that case, we will continue opening new branch offices there," he said.
Generale Bank now has six branch offices there. Chaffart said the bank's aim was to have at least 20 branch offices in NRW, employing a total of about 150 people.
Chaffart said in September 1995 that his bank was looking for an acquisition in Germany, a call he repeated last March.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
